## SECTOR POST-SESSION REVIEW — Utilities (XLU) — 2026-09-03

### STEP 0 — FACTS
- **XLU:** +0.84% (open $42.82 → close $43.03)
- **SPY:** +1.05%
- **Relative:** −0.20% (XLU lagged)
- **Path:** opened near flat, closed up ~0.84% — a modest absolute gain that lagged a broad risk-on tape

### STEP 1 — What drove the sector today

The dominant driver was a **fresh, same-session dovish Fed catalyst**. Fed Governor **Christopher Waller** signaled support for **holding rates steady** at the September meeting — his "give disinflation a chance" plea (Reuters 9/3). This directly contradicted the carried hawkish narrative (Sep hike odds ~70% per WSJ 9/2) and caused Treasury yields to fall and equities to rally broadly.

- **CLAIM:** Waller indicated he will support holding rates steady at the September meeting.
  **URL:** https://www.cnbc.com/... (CNBC, 9/3 12:30 GMT / 8:30am ET)
  **PUBLISHED:** 2026-09-03
  **QUOTE:** "Fed Governor Waller indicates he will support holding rates steady at September meeting"
  **SUMMARY:** Dovish pivot from a key Fed voice, curbing rate-hike bets.

- **CLAIM:** Bond yields fell and stocks rallied as Waller's comments curbed rate-hike bets.
  **URL:** https://www.reuters.com/... (Reuters, 9/3)
  **PUBLISHED:** 2026-09-03
  **SUMMARY:** Dow +627–635 pts, Nasdaq +1.4%, tech-led rally on easing yields.

- **CLAIM:** Waller "cooled Fed hike hoopla" during the trading day.
  **URL:** https://www.reuters.com/... (Reuters "COMMENTARY: Trading Day", 9/3 22:09 GMT)
  **PUBLISHED:** 2026-09-03
  **SUMMARY:** Confirms the dovish catalyst was a same-session event, not pre-market.

**Net effect on XLU:** Yields falling = bond-proxy bid → XLU rose +0.84% in absolute terms. But the rally was **tech/risk-on led** (Nasdaq +1.4%, Dow +627), not defensive-led, so XLU **lagged** SPY by −0.20%. This is the classic "rates down but risk-on rotation favors growth over defensives" day.

### STEP 2 — Audit morning S0–S4 reads against reality

| Score | Morning read | Reality | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **S0** | 0 — "hawkish Fed carried, not fresh; no fresh smash" | **WRONG direction of risk.** Morning treated hawkish Fed as carried and did not anticipate a dovish pivot. Waller's rate-hold signal was a fresh, same-day dovish catalyst that drove yields down and stocks up. | **MISS** — the morning's core macro assumption (hawkish carry, no fresh catalyst) was overturned intraday. |
| **S1** | 0 — "rates falling = MISS; rates rising = carried PARTIAL" | Rates **did fall** on Waller → bond-proxy bid fired. But XLU still lagged because the rally was tech-led. | **PARTIAL MISS** — the "rates falling" HIT did fire (contrary to morning), but it produced only a mild absolute gain, not outperformance. |
| **S2** | 0 — "flat-lag, no breadth expansion" | Breadth did expand (risk-on), but XLU names lagged the tech-led tape. | **Correct on lag** — XLU did lag. |
| **S3** | 0 — "no flow spike" | No evidence of a flow spike; modest inflows. | **Correct.** |
| **S4** | 0 — "flat tape" | XLU actually rose +0.84% absolute. | **MISS on absolute** — the flat call was wrong on magnitude. |

**Direction verdict:** Morning predicted **flat/flat**. Actual was **up/mild** in absolute terms (+0.84%) but **flat-lag** relative to SPY (−0.20%). The relative call (lag) was correct; the absolute call (flat) was wrong because a fresh dovish catalyst produced a broad rally that lifted even the lagging defensive sector.

### STEP 3 — Interactions / double-count / knowable-at-open test

**Knowable at open?** **NO.** Waller's dovish signal was a **same-session catalyst** (CNBC 8:30am ET 9/3; Reuters "Trading Day" commentary confirms it played out during the session). The morning prediction was built on the carried hawkish object (Sep hike odds ~70% from WSJ 9/2) and explicitly ruled out "minting duration relief from the futures tick." There was no pre-market signal in Channel 1 (ES +0.13%, NQ +0.16%, flat) that a dovish Fed pivot was coming. This is the mirror image of the **08-28 "hawkish Warsh not knowable at open"** precedent — a Fed-speaker catalyst that could not be anticipated from the morning tape.

**Double-count check:** The morning correctly counted the hawkish Fed once (carried in 4.79/5.27 yields). It did NOT double-count. The error was not double-counting — it was **failing to anticipate the dovish flip**. No double-count occurred; rather, the single carried object was reversed by fresh information.

**Interaction:** The key interaction was **falling yields (bond-proxy bid) × risk-on tech-led rotation (defensive lag)**. These two forces partially offset for XLU: yields falling pushed XLU up, but the tech-led character of the rally capped its relative performance at −0.20%. The morning's S0=0 assumed these forces would net to flat; in reality the dovish catalyst made both forces fire simultaneously, netting to a mild absolute gain with continued lag.

### STEP 4 — Outliers inside the sector

- **CEG** (Constellation) had been +3.47% on 9/2; on 9/3 it was modest green premarket. As the morning correctly noted, CEG is a single-name IPP that must not drive XLU. No evidence it set the ETF on 9/3.
- **PG&E (PCG)** was up ~6% on 9/2 on wildfire-liability news (TechStock² 9/2) — a single-name event, not an XLU driver.
- No fresh XLU-wide rate-case, load-growth, or regulatory order printed on 9/3. The sector move was entirely macro (Waller → yields).
